evidence.experimental_conditions: Dose: 6.25 µg (20 nmol) in 25 µl acetone:olive oil (4:1); application area 2 cm² on clipped flank; reading at 48 h post-challenge; species: guinea pig; prior sensitization: 1 mg urushiol epicutaneously 15 days before challenge.

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig epicutaneous sensitization test with tolerance induction
evidence.experimental_conditions: Epicutaneous pretreatment with 5-Me-PDC on days 1 and 15; then sensitizing dose of urushiol on day 30; challenge with urushiol on day 44; challenge dose 6.25 µg/2 cm²; reading at 72 h.
evidence.support_text: The results (Table II, Fig 2) clearly demonstrate that epicutaneous application of 5-Me-PDC induces immune tolerance to urushiol in the guinea pig. The maximum 'average response' in this group was only 0.12 which should be compared with the 1.35 value observed with the positive control group at 72 h.
